subject: Tri-series (cricket)
query: what is a tri series in cricket
title: What is a tri-series in cricket? Three teams, one trophy
answer: A tri-series in cricket is a tournament between three national teams. Each team plays the other two, usually once or twice, in a round-robin, and the two teams with the most points meet in a final for the trophy. Tri-series are played in one-day (ODI) or Twenty20 (T20) format.
in_the_news: Tri-series often appear on the schedule before big ICC events, when boards want extra matches for their squads, so the term pops up in fixture lists and TV guides.
body:
"Tri" means three. In a typical tri-series, the round-robin stage gives every team the same number of matches against both opponents. A win earns points, a no-result or tie usually earns a share, and bonus points or net run rate can separate teams that finish level. The top two then play a final, so one team goes home before it.

The format was a staple of Australian summers for decades: the Benson & Hedges World Series and later the Commonwealth Bank Series brought two touring teams to Australia every season until the late 2000s. Today tri-series are less common, because most cricket is played in bilateral series between two countries, but they still return as warm-up events before world tournaments or when a third team joins a tour.

A tri-series is different from a triangular Test series. Tests last up to five days and are usually played two teams at a time; a tri-series nearly always uses the shorter one-day or T20 formats.

faq.a: A series involving three teams, usually ending in a final between the top two.

faq.q: How does a tri-series work in cricket
faq.a: Each team plays the other two in a round-robin, points decide the standings, and the top two teams play a final.

faq.q: What is the difference between a tri-series and a bilateral series
faq.a: A bilateral series is between two teams only; a tri-series includes three.
